arriving_uk.headline: UK customs allowances — arriving from outside the UK

personal_goods.note: Personal goods (other than alcohol and tobacco) up to £390 in value per person, declared on the green channel. £270 if you arrive by private boat or small plane (not a scheduled commercial flight).

alcohol: Sparkling wine, fortified wine (under 22% ABV): 9 litres
You can split the spirits allowance — e.g. 2L spirits + 4.5L sparkling wine.
tobacco: You can split — e.g. 100 cigarettes + 25 cigars.
arriving_uk.cash: Cash equivalent of £10,000 or more must be declared on entry to the UK (one form per person or family).
prohibited: Meat, dairy, and certain other animal products from outside the EU (limited exceptions for personal supply of baby formula/medical/special dietary).
Live animals / endangered species (CITES) without proper paperwork.
Plants, seeds, or cuttings without a phytosanitary certificate (defra rules).
Counterfeit goods, indecent/obscene material, controlled drugs.
Offensive weapons and self-defence sprays (e.g. pepper spray).
arriving_uk.where_to_declare: Use the red channel at customs if you exceed any allowance or carry anything to declare. There are e-declaration options at heathrow.com/customs.

leaving_uk.headline: Leaving the UK — what you can take
leaving_uk.note: There are generally no UK-side limits on what you can take OUT (apart from controlled goods like weapons, drugs, certain meds). Your destination country sets the import limits.
tips: Tax-free shopping for tourists no longer applies in the UK (since 1 January 2021).
Duty-free at the airport (airside) is still tax-removed — but only useful within your destination's allowance.
If you bought VAT-refundable items in shops thinking the airport would refund, there is no such desk. Confirm with retailer.
Going to the EU? EU customs treat you as arriving from a third country. Check the EU allowance for your destination country.
